name: Smoked Cashew Salsa
desc: Cashews smoked over applewood on the stovetop, then blended with chipotles in adobo into a creamy salsa.

source.title: Guacamole with Pistachios & Smoked Cashew Salsa
source.evidence: Same dish: stovetop applewood-smoked cashews in a steamer or colander, blended with seeded chipotles in adobo, sugar, salt, and water; amounts and smoke time differ.

ingredients.raw: 3-4 canned chipotle chiles in adobo, drained and seeded

steps: Soak the wood chips in water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Line the bottom of a heavy stockpot or Dutch oven with foil and pile the chips in the center. Turn on the vent fan. Heat over high until the chips start to smoke.

Set a steamer basket in the pot above the chips and spread the cashews in it in one layer. Cover, lower the heat to medium-low, and smoke 10 to 15 minutes, until the cashews are golden and smell smoky.
Lift out the cashews and pour a little water over the chips to put them out.
Put the cashews in a blender with 3 chipotles, 1 tbsp sugar, a pinch of salt, and 3/4 cup water. Blend until very smooth, 1 to 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust with the remaining chipotle, sugar, salt, or more water until it is the heat and thickness you want. Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 1 week.
tips: Alex Stupak's Empellón version turns the heat off at the first wisp of smoke and smokes 5 oz cashews for 20 minutes, then blends them with 1 cup water, 2 seeded chipotles, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1 tbsp salt.
No-smoke version: Katherine Martinelli toasts the cashews in a dry skillet over medium heat until lightly golden and relies on the chipotles for smoke.
Leave the chipotle seeds and veins in for a hotter salsa.

references.title: Guacamole with Pistachios & Smoked Cashew Salsa
references.usedFor: cashew weight, dousing the chips, week-long fridge life, Empellón amounts and smoke method for the tip
